missing_details: Precise definition of "generalized moonshine" in terms of graded modules and functions
The group under consideration (the Monster group M) and its elements g,h
The assignment of a graded projective representation V(g) for each g∈M
The assignment of a holomorphic function f(g,h,τ) for each commuting pair (g,h)
The six axiomatic properties (grading, projectivity, Hauptmodul/arithmetic nature, conjugation invariance, trace interpretation, SL₂(ℤ) covariance, normalization at the identity)
refined_question:
Does there exist an assignment that to each element g of the Monster group M associates a ℚ-graded complex vector space V(g), which is a projective representation of the centralizer C_M(g), and to each pair of commuting elements (g,h) in M associates a holomorphic function f(g,h,τ) on the upper half-plane, such that:

1. V(g) carries a graded projective action of C_M(g).
2. For each (g,h), f(g,h,τ) is either constant or a genus-zero Hauptmodul for some genus-zero subgroup of SL₂(ℤ).
3. f(g,h,τ) is invariant (up to a scalar) under simultaneous conjugation of (g,h) by elements of M.
4. There is a linear lift of h acting on V(g) whose graded trace expansion ∑_n Tr(h|V(g)_n) q^n equals f(g,h,τ).
5. For every γ=
 (a b
  c d) in SL₂(ℤ), f(g,h,(aτ+b)/(cτ+d)) equals a scalar multiple of f(g^a h^c, g^b h^d, τ).
6. f(g,h,τ) is proportional to the normalized j-function J(τ)−744 if and only if g=h=1.
justification: The problem name alone does not specify the group, the objects V(g) and f(g,h,τ), nor the precise axioms that characterize 'generalized moonshine'. To make it self-contained, one must state the existence question for graded projective Monster‐modules and their associated genus-zero functions satisfying the six properties originally conjectured by Conway–Norton and Norton (1987). This refined question faithfully encapsulates the canonical formulation given in the 'Generalized moonshine' section of the Monstrous moonshine Wikipedia article, without adding or omitting constraints.
